questions.q: Distinguish between the First-Past-The-Post and Proportional Representation electoral systems.
answer: Democracies use different methods to convert votes into seats, of which two are the most important.

answer.text: In the First-Past-The-Post system, the country is divided into constituencies, each electing one representative. The candidate who wins the largest number of votes in a constituency is declared elected, even if they do not secure a majority. India uses this system for the Lok Sabha and the state assemblies. It is simple and usually produces stable governments with a clear local representative.

In Proportional Representation, parties get seats in proportion to the share of votes they receive, so the legislature closely mirrors the wishes of voters. In India this method, using the single transferable vote, is used for the Rajya Sabha and the election of the President.

answer: Thus FPTP stresses simplicity and stability, while PR stresses fairness in reflecting votes.

questions.q: What measures ensure free and fair elections in India?
answer: Free and fair elections are the foundation of Indian democracy, and several measures secure them.

answer.text: Every citizen aged eighteen and above has the right to vote, regardless of wealth, gender, caste or religion, and votes are cast by secret ballot so that no one can be intimidated.

An independent constitutional body, the Election Commission of India, supervises, directs and controls the entire process. It prepares electoral rolls, conducts polls, registers parties and enforces a Model Code of Conduct to keep the contest fair.
Rules on campaigning and expenditure aim to create a level field, and seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Tribes so that weaker sections are represented.

answer: Together these arrangements make Indian elections genuinely free and fair.

questions.q: Why did India adopt universal adult franchise, and what does it signify for democracy?

answer.text: adopted universal adult franchise from its very first general election, a bold decision given widespread poverty and illiteracy.

list: Every adult citizen was given the right to vote, with each vote of equal value
This was granted at once, not gradually as in most older democracies

answer.lead: It signifies deep faith in equality.
answer.text: It affirms that all are equal as citizens.

list: It rejects any distinction of caste, religion, wealth, education or sex in political rights
It gives the poor and marginalised an equal voice, making rulers accountable to all the people

questions.q: What is the role and importance of an independent Election Commission in India?

answer.text: is the independent body that conducts and supervises elections, and its independence is vital for democracy.

list: It prepares electoral rolls, fixes the schedule, and oversees polling and counting
It enforces the Model Code of Conduct and can act against those who break the rules
It is free of the control of the government of the day, so it can act impartially even against the ruling party
This independence gives its conduct of elections the trust of the people and the losing parties alike
